tutorial.overview.organize: Organize mods — drag and drop mods between category columns to sort your load order
tutorial.overview.conflicts: Deep conflict detection — detects data, asset, and level conflicts with actual values shown inline
tutorial.overview.conflictMap: Conflict map — interactive Kenshi world map showing exterior and interior conflict zones
tutorial.overview.aiSort: AI sorting — export your mod list, let AI suggest an order, then import it
tutorial.overview.pinUncat: Actual load order — a panel with the mods that are on, in the order Kenshi loads them; 📌 pin a mod at its position
tutorial.overview.themes: Kenshi theme — toggle between Dark and Kenshi themes in the toolbar
tutorial.overview.packs: Presets — save and load complete mod configurations
tutorial.sorting.1: Drag and drop mods between category columns to sort your load order.
tutorial.sorting.2: Multi-select — Ctrl+click adds or removes one mod, Shift+click picks the range from the last one you clicked (as in Windows Explorer). What you picked in other categories stays picked. Right-click to move them all to a category at once.
tutorial.sorting.3: Group drag — select multiple mods and drag them together.
tutorial.sorting.4: Uncategorized is a normal column (on the left by default) — move it like any other category.
tutorial.sorting.5: Drag column headers to reorder entire categories.
tutorial.categories.1: Add categories with the "+ Add Category" button in the toolbar.
tutorial.categories.2: Category headers — click the name or ✎ to rename, ⇅ to sort, ◀ ▶ to move, plus color, fold and delete buttons. Right-click for the sort and move menu.
tutorial.categories.3: Drag category headers left/right to reorder them. Load order follows category order.
tutorial.categories.4: Reset Categories restores the default category set.
tutorial.packs.1: Go to the Packs tab to save and load complete mod configurations.
tutorial.packs.2: Save Current keeps it all: on/off, category layout and mod order, the actual load order (📌 priority), 🚫 don't-load and sort rules.
tutorial.packs.3: Load a preset to instantly restore a previous configuration.
tutorial.packs.4: Great for switching between different playthroughs or saving before AI sort.
tutorial.importExport.1: Export List — saves your full setup (categories, load order, active/inactive state) to a text file. Share it with friends or back it up.
tutorial.importExport.2: Import ▾ — Import… (Ctrl+O) a BEEP mod list file, Import from String… (Ctrl+I), or open a list in the Mod List Viewer (Ctrl+Shift+O).
tutorial.importExport.3: Generic import — also supports plain lists of .mod filenames (one per line). These reorder your uncategorized mods to match the list.
tutorial.conflicts.1: Check Conflicts deep-parses .mod files, level data, and asset files to find real conflicts.
tutorial.conflicts.2: Green = this mod wins, Red = overridden, Yellow = both overridden by a third mod.
tutorial.conflicts.3: Expand any property to see the actual values each mod sets. Identical values are filtered out.
tutorial.conflicts.4: Click Map to see conflicts on the Kenshi world map with zoom, pan, and exterior/interior toggle.
tutorial.other.1: Themes — toggle Dark/Kenshi theme in the toolbar.
tutorial.other.2: Workshop tab — browse Steam Workshop directly in the app.
tutorial.other.3: Modding Guide tab — Kenshi load order guide from Steam.
tutorial.other.4: Updates — Help → Check for Updates…; Help → Check for Updates on Start turns the check at launch on or off.
tutorial.aiSort.desc: AI Sort uses an AI chatbot (Claude or ChatGPT) to automatically sort your mods into the correct Kenshi load order.
tutorial.aiSort.1: Save a preset first in the Presets tab so you can revert.
tutorial.aiSort.2: Click AI Sort Export — fetches Steam descriptions and builds a text file.
tutorial.aiSort.3: Paste the file into an AI chatbot and send it.
tutorial.aiSort.5: Click AI Sort Import, paste, and click Apply Order.
tutorial.aiSort.privacy: No data is sent automatically — you are the middleman. The app only contacts Steam's public API for descriptions.
tutorial.aiExport.1: Uncategorized Only — unsorted mods with full descriptions (recommended)
tutorial.aiExport.3: All Mods Compact — everything with short descriptions (500+ mods)
tutorial.aiExport.4: All Mods Full — complete descriptions (most accurate, largest)
tutorial.aiExport.5: Split Batches — multiple files with ~50 mods each
tutorial.aiExport.formatNote: Extra commentary is OK — the parser strips everything that isn't a [Category] header or a .mod filename.
tutorial.sorting.6: Actual load order panel (left) — the mods that are on, in the order Kenshi loads them. Drop a mod there to put it at that position: it gets a 📌 pin. Right-click to pin / unpin; ⟲ above the panel unpins all.
tutorial.sorting.7: Fold buttons on the bars between the panels fold and unfold the side panels.
tutorial.sorting.8: Keyboard — Ctrl+X / Ctrl+V move, Shift+↑/↓ one step, Shift+←/→ previous / next category, Ctrl+Shift+↑/↓ top / bottom, F8 / Shift+F8 next / previous mod with a problem, Ctrl+Z undo, Ctrl+S save (the view follows the moved category). All keys: File → Shortcut Keys….
tutorial.categories.5: ⚙ Settings (Ctrl+,) — the category layout (Workshop tags, BEEP defaults or your own list), sort rules, category width, scroll speed and the Kenshi folders.
tutorial.importExport.4: Share as a string — in Advanced Export… (Ctrl+Shift+E) pick the format String: the whole list becomes one line starting with BEEP1:. Copy it to the clipboard or save it as txt. The other side pastes it (or opens the txt) in Import from String… and imports it into the main screen or opens it in the viewer.
tutorial.viewer.1: Mod List Viewer… (Ctrl+Shift+O, also in Import ▾) opens an exported list or string in its own window. Your current setup isn't touched; up to 4 windows at once.
tutorial.viewer.2: View mode only shows the list; Edit mode lets you turn mods on / off, move them, and add, rename or delete categories.
tutorial.viewer.3: Addable owned mods (left, folded at first) — mods you have that the list doesn't; drag them in.
tutorial.viewer.4: Mods you don't have can be subscribed to on the Workshop. Import to main screen applies the list; Export ▾ saves it again as a file or string (named …_사본 01 and so on).
tutorial.viewer.5: Ctrl+M minimize, Ctrl+Shift+M maximize / restore, F11 full screen. Unsaved changes are asked about when you close it.
tutorial.translator.1: Open it with Ctrl+T, File → Translate / Patch Tool…, or right-click mods → Open in the Translate / Patch Tool…. It runs in its own window; Ctrl+T / Esc put it down again.
tutorial.translator.2: It reads the text in .mod files and translates it: your glossary first, then a translation the mod already has (main.po), the rest by Google Translate (with waits and a cache, so a stopped job goes on where it left off).
tutorial.translator.3: Three ways to save: a separate patch mod (_KO, the original untouched), editing the original (backed up first), or a field-copy patch (_Patch). Right-clicking mods also offers the patch mod and the field-copy patch directly.
tutorial.translator.4: Extract writes the text that needs translating into a glossary file (source =, dialogue grouped by PACKAGE › DIALOGUE › LINE) to fill in elsewhere. A source with = in it is written source =|= translation.
tutorial.translator.5: Translation review — check and fix translations line by line and add them to the glossary. The newest 5 files are on the left; older ones are grouped by mod, with a search.
tutorial.translator.6: Finished mods show [Done] name date time [KO] [Bak] [Patch] [Glo]: click one to open the file (a .mod opens in FCS). The target language follows the app language and can be changed in the tool's ⚙ Settings.
tutorial.overview.viewer: Mod list viewer — open a shared list in its own window, look it over or edit it, then import it
tutorial.overview.share: Share strings — your whole list as one BEEP1: line to paste anywhere
tutorial.overview.translator: Translate / patch tool — translate mods with a glossary and Google, make patch mods, review the results
tutorial.categories.6: 🚫 Don't load — a category's 🚫 button (or right-click → Don't load) keeps its mods out of the game: they leave mods.cfg, and whether each was on is kept (a dashed box) for when it moves to another category. Uncategorized starts with 🚫 on a new setup, so new mods don't load until you sort them.
noLoad.tipOff: Don't load this category: its mods stay out of the game (whether each is on is kept for when it leaves)
noLoad.tipOn: This category doesn't load (🚫). Click to load it again
noLoad.on: "{name}" no longer loads: its mods are out of the game.
noLoad.parkedTip: This category doesn't load (🚫). The box says whether the mod is on once it leaves the category.
noLoad.firstRun: Mods that are on are in Uncategorized, so it still loads. Its 🚫 button keeps new mods from loading until you sort them.
cm.noLoadTip: Its mods stay out of the game; whether each is on is kept for when it leaves
aiExport.uncatDesc: Only fetches descriptions for mods in Uncategorized. Already-sorted mods are listed by filename only. Much smaller file, faster AI processing, lower cost.
aiExport.uncatCompactDesc: Only unsorted mods, using tags + truncated descriptions. Already-sorted mods listed by filename. Best balance of accuracy and size.
aiExport.compactDesc: All mods using Steam tags + first 200 characters. Fits 500+ mods in a single prompt. Use for a full re-sort without exceeding token limits.
aiExport.allDesc: Fetches full descriptions for every active mod. Most accurate but produces a very large file. May exceed AI token limits for 100+ mods.
aiExport.splitDesc: Exports multiple files with ~50 mods each (full descriptions). Run each through the AI separately. Most accurate but most tedious.
order.title: Actual Load Order
order.tip: The order Kenshi loads mods (top = loaded first). Drag here to place a mod at a position; it moves into the category it lands in.
edit.needFocus: Click a category or the load order list first.
edit.picked: {count} mods picked to move — click where they should go and press Ctrl+V (Esc cancels).
edit.clipEmpty: Nothing to paste. Pick mods with Ctrl+X first.
edit.askTop: Put the mods at the top or the bottom of "{cat}"?
unsaved.saveTip: There are unsaved changes — press to save.
unsaved.refreshText: Changes made since the last save haven't been saved. Refresh takes the load order, the mods' places and the categories (order, names, colors) back to the last saved state.
unsaved.closeText: Changes made since the last save haven't been saved. Save before closing?
imp.presetDesc.all: Categories, places, load order and on/off as in the file
imp.presetDesc.fill: Mine stay as they are; missing mods go to their category in the file
imp.presetDesc.uncat: Mine stay as they are; missing mods go to Uncategorized
imp.presetNoCats: Not available: the file has no categories
imp.loadTip: Subscribed / downloaded mods can come in on or off by themselves. On refresh they are set as chosen here. (On: the ones on in the file)
imp.d.place: Places and load order of my mods
imp.v.missing.file: Their category and place in the file
imp.sum.missing.file: missing → their place in the file
sb.totalTip: Installed mods (placeholders to subscribe to / download not counted)
sb.problemsTip: Mods with errors / warnings — click to go to the first (F8)
sb.subscribeTip: Mods to subscribe to — click to open the subscribe queue
sb.downloadTip: Listed but not installed — click to download them
sb.pinnedTip: Mods pinned in the load order — click to select them
sb.clipTip: Mods picked up to move — paste with {key}. Click to select them
sb.zoomTip: Zoom — click to go back to 100%
sb.updatesTip: Mods with an update — click to open Updates
sb.gameTip: Version of the Factorio game found
sb.conflictsTip: Mods that are on with conflicts in the last check — click to select them
sb.linksTip: Steam mods linked into the game folder — click to select them
sb.mapTip: The map mod that is on — click to go to it
sb.pendingTip: Mods that are on but not installed / updated yet (the game gets them when it starts) — click to select them
cm.shiftAdds: Hold Shift to add to the selection
cm.unusable: Mods this game version can't use
sortEdit.nameTip: Click to rename · press and hold, then drag to reorder
sortEdit.dragTip: Press and hold, then drag to reorder
sortEdit.deleteTip: Delete the category (on Apply; its mods go to Uncategorized)
sortEdit.hint: Click a color or name to change it, press and hold a row and drag to reorder, ✕ to delete. Nothing changes until Apply.
sortRule.title: Sort
sortRule.desc: Set a default sort rule, then choose default, custom or no sorting for each category. Mods are sorted by their original name. If the order of mods that are on changes, you are asked whether the actual load order should follow.
sortRule.defAuto: Turn auto sort on for categories that start using the default
sortRule.applyAllTip: Switch every category to the default rule and sort it now (auto sort follows the checkbox above)
sortRule.autoTip: On: re-sorted as soon as mods are moved (mouse, keyboard, shortcuts) or turned on/off. Off: sorted once, then mods stay where you put them.
sortRule.nowTip: Sort this category when you press Apply
sortRule.classesTip: Order of character kinds in names. Change with ◀ ▶. (Direction does not change this order.)
sortRule.autoOff: Auto sort off for "{name}". You can now move mods freely.
sortRule.autoKept: "{name}" is auto-sorted, so it keeps its sort order. Turn auto sort off with ⇅ in its header to arrange it by hand.
sortRule.orderTitle: Apply to the actual load order too?
sortRule.orderAsk:
Sorting changes the order of the mods that are on in: {names}.

Apply to actual order: the load order saved to mods.cfg is sorted too.
Sort category only: the actual load order stays as it is; mods out of line are pinned (📌).
pin.tip: Pinned: its place in the load order was set by hand and stays put when categories change.
pin.pinned: Pinned {count} mods at their current load order position.
pin.unpinned: Unpinned {count} mods — they follow their category again.
pin.resetText: Unpin all {count} pinned mods and put the load order back in category order?
pin.resetDone: All pins removed: the load order follows the categories.
pin.resetTip: Unpin all 📌 mods (load order follows the categories)
catMove.title: Move pinned mods too?
catMove.text:
"{name}" has {count} mods pinned (📌) to a place in the load order.

Move them along: they lose their pin and move with the category.
Keep them in place: they stay where they are in the load order.
sortRule.orderTip: Whether auto sort also changes the actual load order
toolbar.autoClassifyTip: File Uncategorized mods by their Steam Workshop tags (and names), leftmost category first
scheme.resetDesc: Clears all categories and builds new ones. Mods stay on/off, presets are kept, and Undo brings it back.
scheme.tagsDesc: GUI, Graphical, Translation, RE_Kenshi, Races, Characters, Factions, Buildings, Clothing/Armour, Items/Weapons, Research, Gameplay, Cheats, Total Overhaul.
scheme.classicDesc: UI & graphics, Animations, Races, Animals, Game starts, Factions, Buildings, Armor & weapons, Overhauls, Patches, Economy.
scheme.listNote: Top of the list = left = loads first and gets mods first when classifying.
scheme.listEmpty: No categories to create. Add some below.
scheme.autoTip: Gets the Workshop tags of Steam mods (needs internet) and files each mod into the first matching category; BEEP defaults also use mod names.
scheme.hideEmpty: Skip categories that would have no mods
scheme.keepOrder: Keep the current actual load order
scheme.keepOrderTip: On: the order in mods.cfg stays; mods out of line with the new categories are pinned (📌). Off: the load order follows the new categories.
settings.unsavedText: Some settings were changed but not saved.
detail.copies: Other copies with this file name: {count}
detail.copiesNote: Each copy can be placed and sorted on its own. Kenshi loads mods by file name, so only one copy can be on — turning one on turns the others off.
card.copies: {count} mods with the same file name (only one can be on)
copies.oneOn: Only one copy of a mod name can be on (mods.cfg stores names): "{name}" stays on, its other copies were turned off.
detail.neededByTip: Mods that list this mod as a dependency or reference
detail.jumpTip: Click to go to this mod
detail.dependenciesTip: Mods this mod needs (its "dependencies"): they must be on and load before it.
detail.referencesTip: Mods whose data this mod uses (its "references", as set by the mod author): they should load before it.
deps.warnAfter: must load before this mod : dependency warning
deps.warnBefore: set to load first : dependency warning
deps.placeAfter: Send right after its required mod
deps.placeAfterTip: Puts this mod right after the last required/referenced mod that loads after it, and pins it there.
deps.placed: Sent "{name}" right after "{after}" (#{pos}) and pinned it.
order.notInOrder: "{name}" is off, so it is not in the actual load order.
catNav.title: Categories
catNav.jumpTip: Click to go to this category
detail.nameLinkTip: Click to open the Steam Workshop page
detail.fcsTip: Click to open this file in the FCS (Forgotten Construction Set)
detail.fcsNotFound: Could not find "forgotten construction set.exe" in the game folder.
detail.fileNotFound: Could not find the mod file.
menu.selLeft: Select in the list to the left
menu.selRight: Select in the list to the right
keys.title: Shortcut keys
keys.desc: Click a key box, then press the new key (Space, F1–F12, A–Z, digits, arrows and other keys, alone or with Ctrl / Shift / Alt). Press Save to keep the changes.
keys.settingsDesc: Change the keyboard shortcuts shown in the Edit menu.
keys.movedFrom: {key} was used by {action}; that one now has no key.
keys.resetAllText: Put every shortcut key back to its default?
keys.deleteText:
Move the files of these {count} mod(s) to the Recycle Bin?
(This does not delete them for good: to delete them completely, also delete them from the Recycle Bin or empty it.)
keys.deleteSteamNote: Steam Workshop mods are downloaded again by Steam while you are subscribed. To remove them completely, unsubscribe on their Workshop pages.
keys.deleted: Moved {count} mod(s) to the Recycle Bin (empty the Recycle Bin to delete them for good). Save to update the load order.
keys.unsubText: {count} Workshop mod(s) were deleted. Steam will download them again unless you unsubscribe. Open their Workshop pages?
keys.menuFixed: View / Window menu (fixed, can't be changed)
keys.reserved: {key} is already used by {place}, so it can't be used here.
menuBar.fixed: The menu bar is always shown.
menuBar.hidden: The menu bar is hidden. Press Alt to show it.
category.shrinkTip: Shrink: make the column only as wide as its mod names need, up to the set width (click again to undo)
category.expandTip: Widen: make the column wide enough to show every mod name in full (click again to undo)
settings.autoShrink: Shrink category columns to fit the mod names
settings.autoShrinkNote: Off keeps the set width. Each category can choose with its →← / ⇼ buttons; Reset turns ⇼ (widen) off.
reset.tip: Put every setting back to the start and begin again from the first-start screen (game folder, language)
reset.title: Reset settings
reset.text:
Every setting goes back to the start, and the screen for choosing the game folders and language comes up as on a first start. (Presets stay; game files are not changed.)

What about the categories?
reset.unsaved: Unsaved load order changes will be lost.
sq.title: Workshop subscribe queue
sq.desc: These mods are not installed. Subscribe on the page on the right and Steam downloads them. Log in to Steam in the right pane once.
sq.steamTip: Open this mod's Workshop page in the Steam client (already logged in)
sq.autoTip: Click each page's Subscribe button in turn, slowly, with the logged-in account
sq.searchNote: The Workshop id is unknown, so this is a search. Pick the right mod and subscribe.
sq.notLoggedIn: Not logged in to Steam. Log in with "login" at the top of the page on the right.
sq.closed: Closed the subscribe queue ({n} subscribed). Refresh once Steam has downloaded them.
sq.buttonTip: Open the mods that need subscribing in the Workshop subscribe queue (subscribed ones are not counted)
sq.autoSetting: Allow "Subscribe to all" in the subscribe queue
sq.autoSettingNote: Adds a "Subscribe to all" button to the queue. The app then clicks Subscribe for you with your logged-in Steam account, so turn it on only if you want that.
imp.title: Import settings
imp.modeAll: Import everything (categories, placement, load order, on/off)
imp.modeMods: Import mods only (my categories and load order stay, new mods go to Uncategorized)
imp.modeList: Turn on and order as listed (new mods go to Uncategorized)
imp.subscribeNote: Mods that are not installed can be subscribed to in the subscribe queue after importing.
imp.done: Imported. {n} changed mod(s) are marked in colour (the marks go when you save).
imp.subscribeAsk: {n} mod(s) are not installed. Open the subscribe queue?
imp.modeModsKenshi: Import mods only (my categories and load order stay; on/off only)
sq.autoSettingNoteKenshi: Adds a "Subscribe to all" button to the queue (for mods with a Workshop id). The app then clicks Subscribe for you with your logged-in Steam account, so turn it on only if you want that.
ghost.queueTip: Click to open the Workshop subscribe queue
ghost.installTip: Click to download from the mod portal
ghost.pendingTip: Subscribed. Refresh once Steam has downloaded it and it becomes an installed mod.
ghost.moveTip: Drag it, or click it and use Shift+arrows. Once installed the mod goes into this place.
keys.deleteTextUndo:
Delete the files of these {count} mod(s)?
(Undo (Ctrl+Z) brings them back. They go to the Recycle Bin when the app closes; empty it to delete them for good.)
keys.deletedUndo: Deleted {count} mod(s). Undo (Ctrl+Z) brings them back; they go to the Recycle Bin when the app closes. Save to update the load order.
keys.ghostsRemoved: Took {count} not-installed mod(s) off the list (Undo brings them back).
keys.deleteGhostsToo: The {count} selected not-installed mod(s) are only taken off the list.
keys.deleteFolderNote: {count} unpacked (folder) mod(s) go to the Recycle Bin at once and can't be undone.
sq.keys: Keys: W/↑ A/← previous mod, S/↓ D/→ next mod (also after clicking the page)
sq.rateLimited: Steam refused for a moment (too many requests). Loading again in 30 seconds; the wait is now {s} s for this window.
sq.rateLimitedAuto: Steam refused for a moment. Waiting a minute, then going on…
keys.restoreGone: The files of "{name}" are already gone, so they can't come back. It stays in its place as a mod that isn't installed.
sq.gapInfo: Waits {s} s between pages ({n} mods). You can change this in Settings.
sq.gapNone: Only {n} mods, so pages open without waiting. You can change this in Settings.
sq.holdGap: Waiting a moment between pages so Steam doesn't refuse with "too many requests". You can move to another mod meanwhile — only the one you stop on opens.
sq.holdRetry: Steam refused for a moment ("too many requests"). It loads again after the wait. The wait between pages is longer for this window now.
sq.nowWarn: Opening without waiting may make Steam show "Sorry! You've made too many requests recently" and refuse for a while.
sq.noAsk: Don't ask again in this window
sq.gapByCount: Scale with the number of mods (under 5: no wait, 5–9: half, 10 or more: all of it)
sq.gapNote: Steam refuses for a while ("too many requests") when many pages open in a short time. The default is 6 seconds (2.5 seconds was refused after about ten).
sq.gapLowText: With {s} seconds Steam may block the pages with "Sorry! You've made too many requests recently". Then you have to wait from 30 seconds to a few minutes. (Default: {d} seconds)
sq.settingsTip: Workshop subscribe settings (wait between pages, Subscribe to all)
sq.settingsSaved: Changes apply at once and are kept in the app's Settings too.
ghost.noWsTip: The Workshop id of this mod is unknown (a manually installed mod, for example). The subscribe queue shows a search by its name.
steam.forgot: Took {count} mods whose folder is gone out of Steam's Workshop record. After Steam restarts it downloads the subscribed ones again.
steam.forgotRunning: (If Steam is running, quit it completely and start it again.)
steam.forgetFailed: Could not update Steam's Workshop record: {error}
imp.modeDesc.all: Categories, placement and load order as in the import (missing categories are made).
imp.modeDesc.fill: My layout stays; only mods I don't have go to their place (missing categories are made).
imp.modeDesc.mods: Mods I don't have go to Uncategorized (no categories are made).
imp.optMissing: Show mods I don't have too (to subscribe and install)
imp.optNewOn: When a missing mod is installed:
imp.boardTip: Every category is shown. Drag mods to the top / after the mods that are on / the bottom. Ctrl/Shift+click (or a category, then Ctrl+A) picks several to drag at once, or Ctrl+X (or C) picks them up and a click on a place puts them there. Drag a new category's header onto another category to merge it.
imp.mergeTip: Drop it on another category to move all its mods there.
imp.zone.afterActive: after the mods that are on
imp.optKeepOff: Don't turn on mods that are off now
imp.optKeepOn: Don't turn off mods that are on now (wins over "turn off mods that aren't in the file")
imp.optTurnOn: Turn on my mods that are on in the file
imp.boardTipView: Only categories with mods that change or come in are shown. Turn on "Custom edit" to place them yourself.
imp.clipTip: Click where the {n} mods go, or click a mod in the target category and press Ctrl+V (its bottom). Esc cancels.
imp.pasteWhere: Click a place, or click a mod in the target category and press Ctrl+V.
imp.selectAllWhere: Click a category first (Ctrl+A selects all of its mods).
imp.optKeepPlace: Keep my mods where they are (the import doesn't move them)
vw.editTip: Move mods and categories, turn mods on / off, add, rename and delete categories
vw.viewNote: View mode — press [Edit] to change it
vw.editNote: Edit mode — your own setup isn't changed (Save As)
vw.pool: Owned mods not in this list
vw.poolTip: The mods you have that this list doesn't. In Edit mode drag one into a category to add it; drag it back here to take it out
vw.subTitle: Subscribe to missing mods
vw.subText: This puts {n} mods into the main window's subscribe queue.
vw.subSent: Put {n} mods into the main window's subscribe queue
vw.importTip: Opens this list in the main window's import settings (nothing is applied before you choose)
vw.imported: Opened the import settings in the main window
vw.refreshTip: Reads the installed mods and your own list again (mods you subscribed to come in)
vw.editOnly: This is View mode — press [Edit] at the top to change things
vw.poolViewNote: View mode — press [Edit] to drag them in
vw.poolEditNote: Drag one into a category to add it to the list
vw.exportTip: Exports this list as a new file (name_copy 01.txt); this window becomes that file
vw.removed: Took {n} out of the list (now in Owned mods you can add, on the left)
vw.max: Up to {n} list windows can be open. Close one and open this again.
vw.closeText: Changes in {name} aren't saved. Save them under a new name?
vw.title: Mod List Viewer
toolbar.importMoreTip: Mod List Viewer: look at and edit an exported list in its own window (your setup isn't changed)
exp.strHint: The app's file as one string starting with 'BEEP1:'. In a chat app, send it inside a code block (```) so its symbols aren't turned into formatting. Import ▾ → Import from String brings it back.
exp.strCopied: Copied the string to the clipboard ({n} chars)
strImp.title: Import from String
strImp.text: Paste a mod list string starting with 'BEEP1:'. (``` around it and line breaks are ignored)
strImp.fromClip: Put in the string from the clipboard
strImp.ok: A good mod list — {n} mods · {c} categories · saved {when}
strImp.saved: Saved as a mod list file: {path}
strImp.err.other: This is a {game} mod list string. Import it in the {game} mod manager.
strImp.err.prefix: This isn't a mod list string (it must start with 'BEEP1:').
strImp.err.chars: The string has letters it can't have. Part of it may have changed while copying (chat formatting etc.).
strImp.err.zlib: It can't be unpacked. The string is cut off or changed.
strImp.err.notList: It unpacked, but it isn't a mod list.
kmt.dockTip: Open / minimize the Translate / Patch Tool (Ctrl+T)
kmt.openWith: Open in the Translate / Patch Tool…
kmt.started: Started in the Translate / Patch Tool ({count} mods)
kmt.opened: Added {count} mods to the Translate / Patch Tool
kmt.placedOn: Made '{name}', put it in '{cat}' and turned it on — save to apply it to the game
kmt.placedEarly: '{name}' is in '{cat}' but loads before '{original}' — move it after the original for the patch to work
kmt.editedOriginal: Translated '{name}' in place (the original is kept as .bak)
kmt.madeElsewhere: Made '{name}': {path} (not in the game's mods folder, so not in the list)
exp.title: Advanced export
exp.noCatsNote: Without categories the file can only be imported as "Mods only".
toolbar.exportMoreTip: Advanced export (or press and hold Export)
imp.optOffAbsent: Turn off my mods that aren't in the file
exp.pickBanner: Advanced export in progress… Pick the mods for "Selected mods only" (each click on a mod or category header adds or removes). Closing the panel brings everything back.
exp.quickLinksTip: Copies the names and links of the mods that are on
exp.pickHint: Each click adds or removes a mod or a category header. Shift: the first click turns one over, the next ones turn over what lies between. Drag from empty space (or from a mod with a key held): a box (Shift adds, Alt removes, Ctrl or Shift+Alt turns over). Ctrl+Z/Y: selection undo, Esc: clear.
exp.pickHintShort: While this panel is open the main screen only selects (mods, category headers).
exp.shareNote: A list for Discord or forums. To import it again, save the app file instead.
exp.copied: Copied the link list of {n} mods.
